statement: Water is pumped out of a pond at a constant rate. Three hours after pumping starts, the pond holds $1{,}155$ gallons of water. Eight hours after pumping starts, it holds $980$ gallons. If the pumping continues at the same rate, how many hours after pumping starts will the pond be empty?

choices.misconception: I found the rate of 35 gallons per hour and divided the 980 gallons by 35 to get 28, but that is the time after the 8-hour mark, not after pumping started.
I divided the 1,155 gallons by 35 to get 33 hours, but that counts from the 3-hour mark, so I forgot to add the 3 hours already gone.
I thought the pond started with only 35 gallons more than at 3 hours, so I used $1{,}190$ gallons and got $1{,}190 \div 35 = 34$.

hints: First find how many gallons leave the pond each hour.
Use the rate to find how much water was in the pond at the start, then find when that amount reaches zero.
In the $5$ hours between the readings, $175$ gallons left, so $35$ gallons per hour. At the start there were $1{,}155 + 3(35) = 1{,}260$ gallons.

solutions.reliable: The rate is $\dfrac{1{,}155 - 980}{8 - 3} = \dfrac{175}{5} = 35$ gallons per hour. At $t = 0$ the pond held $1{,}155 + 3(35) = 1{,}260$ gallons, so $W(t) = 1{,}260 - 35t$. Setting $W(t) = 0$ gives $t = 1{,}260 \div 35 = 36$ hours.
solutions.elegant: At hour $8$ there are $980$ gallons left, which takes $980 \div 35 = 28$ more hours to pump out. The pond is empty at $8 + 28 = 36$ hours.
